topic: federal carbon tax and universal rebate
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Kessering paired its carbon levy with a universal quarterly payment set at the median household's fuel cost, not the mean. Ninety-one percent of households in the bottom two income quintiles came out ahead in the first year, because the median is the number that protects the typical payer while the mean is dragged upward by the largest emitters.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Vantborough ring-fenced a third of carbon receipts for public transport rather than returning all of it. Ridership rose 24 percent over four years, and the province's fuel demand fell faster than in neighbouring Kessering, which rebated everything. Spending some of the revenue beat rebating all of it.

topic: carbon tax harm to low income households
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. The harm a carbon tax does to a low-income household is concentrated in the months before the first rebate arrives. Kessering's own review found the gap was eliminated by paying the first instalment one month ahead of the levy taking effect, at a one-off cost of 0.3 percent of annual receipts.

topic: federal carbon tax and rural households
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Rural households in Kessering drove 40 percent further per week than urban ones and so paid more levy per head. A rural supplement worth 1.6 times the base payment closed the gap without exempting anyone, which kept the price signal intact for every driver.

topic: carbon tax good for industrial transition
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Vantborough's transition fund retrained 4,100 workers from two closing plants over six years, financed entirely from levy receipts. Regional unemployment ended the period 1.2 points below the national figure, against 2.4 points above it when the plants closed.
